boundaries: TOY-EVIDENCE on one deterministic instance at each of 15, 17, and 19 field bits.
The accepted subgroup orders were 10799, 9851, and 129737; fitted exponents are not interpretable because q was non-monotone and B took only two values.
The result covers only the frozen x-interval, square-map, and rational-union definitions.
No result establishes a generic-prime-field barrier, a faster-than-rho algorithm, or deployment relevance.
evidence.inference: NEGATIVE RESULT: no tested coordinate family met the frozen energy, target-coverage, and offline-cost gate at two sizes. OBSERVATION: random target coverage follows an unordered-multiset occupancy model far more closely than the preregistered ordered-tuple Poisson model. High pair energy alone compressed joins but reduced target support in the scalar-progression control.
observations: All coordinate families had exactly 1.0x the random-control pair additive energy at all three sizes.
No coordinate family reached 1.5x random target success at any size; rational_union reached 1.25x only at 19 field bits.
The scalar-progression positive control reached up to 2.616x random pair energy but succeeded on zero of 128 targets at two sizes.
Observed random target coverage was 0.0703, 0.0703, and 0.0313; unordered-multiset predictions were 0.0707, 0.0773, and 0.0331.
The independent verifier recomputed three curve orders, all factor-base schedules and sum counters, all five-term witnesses, and 24 Pollard-rho outputs.
unresolved_confounds: One seed and 128 targets per size leave substantial binomial uncertainty in target-success ratios.
Sign-complete factor bases induce cancellation and permutation dependencies that need explicit comparison with sign-canonical formulations.
The Python deep-size metric is implementation-specific and was not independently interpreted as a machine-independent storage bound.
The generator run retained unexpected AppleDouble metadata artifacts; arithmetic raw data and its hash were independently verified unchanged.
